summary: Backend-only verification completed for Internal AI BRSR routing regressions. Focused deterministic regression (3 tests) and live admin flow (3 prompts in one test) passed.
action_items: No blocking fix required for the requested BRSR regression scope.
Optional auth hardening: add httpOnly cookie session support if required by product policy.
Optional auth hardening: implement explicit brute-force lockout after 5 failed attempts per account (distinct from generic per-IP rate limiting).
Optional CORS hardening: avoid allow_origins=['*'] when allow_credentials=true in production-like deployments.
critical_code_review_comments: modules/auth/router.py returns tokens in JSON only; no Set-Cookie/httpOnly cookie is set on login route.
Auth flow uses slowapi limiter (10/minute) but there is no account-scoped 5-failure lockout path in modules/auth/router.py.
server.py CORS fallback sets allow_origins ['*'] while allow_credentials=True; this is a risky configuration and should be restricted to explicit origins.
backend/server.py remains very large (>700 lines), increasing regression risk and test surface complexity.
test_credentials: Read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md and matched supplied admin credentials.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Requested BRSR routing failure cases are not reproducible now. Live checks passed for generic filled-count, bare 2026-2027 FY mapping, and training-coverage version history query with unique session_id per request.
rca of the issue: Original issue appears resolved by deterministic routing/period logic now present in query_understanding.py, reporting_periods.py, and brsr service. Verified outcomes: query_type brsr_lookup for both count prompts, non-zero 6/165 counts, FY label in response for 2026-2027, and query_type brsr_version_history with non-empty history signal for training coverage prompt.
